prompt: A tree casts a shadow $20$ ft long. From the tip of the shadow, the angle of elevation up to the top of the tree is $45^\circ$. How tall is the tree, in feet?
hint: Draw the right triangle: the shadow is the bottom side and the tree is the upright side.

hints.text: Draw the right triangle: the shadow is the bottom side and the tree is the upright side.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $10$ ft shadow with a $45^\circ$ elevation gives a $10$ ft pole, because $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$ makes height equal shadow. Same move, bigger number.
Seen from the shadow tip, the tree is opposite the angle and the shadow is adjacent, so use tangent: $\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{h}{20}$.
Since $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, we get $\frac{h}{20} = 1$, so the tree is $h = 20$ ft tall.

explanation: An angle of elevation is measured UP from the flat ground to the line of sight.
The tree is opposite that angle and the shadow is adjacent, so TOA gives $\tan(45^\circ) = \frac{h}{20}$.
Because $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, the height equals the shadow length, so the tree is $h = 20$ ft tall.

alternativeExplanations.title: It is a 45-45-90 triangle
steps: One angle is $90^\circ$ and another is $45^\circ$, so the last angle is $180 - 90 - 45 = 45$ degrees too.
Two equal angles make the sides across from them equal, so the two legs match.
The shadow leg is $20$ ft, so the tree leg is also $20$ ft.

alternativeExplanations.title: Scale up a small model
steps: Model the scene with a $1$ ft stick: at a $45^\circ$ sun angle its rise equals its run, so its shadow is $1$ ft.
The tree and its shadow make the same shape as the stick and its shadow, only larger.
The tree's shadow is $20$ times the stick's shadow, so the tree is $20 \times 1 = 20$ ft tall.
